# Behavioral Canarying for Prompt Injection

Archival repository for a Hermes Labs Zenodo technical note. Read the paper
at https://hermes-labs.ai/research/behavioral-canarying or cite the DOI
directly.

## What this is

A pre-execution prompt-injection sensing architecture: untrusted input is
deliberately exposed to a powerless language-model probe, and its response is
examined for evidence of behavioral compromise before an authority-bearing
agent acts. The central contribution is an evidence-preserving interface that
separates routing disposition from inspection coverage, so a fail-open route
taken because inspection failed can never be conflated with a route taken
because inspection ran and found nothing.

## Evidence boundary

This note does not claim universal detection, formal security, aggregate
accuracy for the current release, or invention of the general
sacrificial-canary concept. It names the closest located prior art
(Sibylline Software's canary-agent design) rather than claiming novelty over
it, and reports no numeric detection or false-positive rate for the current
release.

## Not affiliated

Hermes Labs is not affiliated with NousResearch, Teknium, the Nous-Hermes LLM
line, or the unrelated `hermes-agent` project.
